assertions.text: event(billing).published where order_id == {{ORDER_ID}} within cross_service exists

corpus_findings.detail: Positive assertion on a stimulus-produced subject with a per-execution-unique correlator, outside a control block, with no bracketing wrapper in the scenario. method/12 H1.

fragment_A.why: Correct evaluator behavior on a defective specification. `exists` is true of one message and equally true of two — it cannot fail on a duplicate. The verdict is right; the corpus finding is what carries the signal.

assertions.text: event(billing).published where order_id == {{ORDER_ID}} within cross_service count == 1

corpus_findings.detail: count == 1 with appearance semantics. Satisfied at 120ms; the duplicate at 4100ms arrives after polling stopped. Catches only a simultaneous duplicate, never a delayed one.

fragment_B.why: The load-bearing fragment. `count == 1` is the obvious repair and it is still wrong — the receipt carve-out correctly assigns `within`, `within` is first-true-wins, and the evaluator stops looking before the duplicate lands. An evaluator that returns FAIL here has mis-implemented `within` as `hold` (see case 001).

assertions.text: event(billing).published where order_id == {{ORDER_ID}} within cross_service count == 1
event(billing).published where order_id == {{ORDER_ID}} hold single_hop count == 1

fragment_C.why: The pair. The receipt bounds the count upward from nothing and passes; the bracket bounds it forward in time and catches the delayed duplicate. Both assertions are recorded — the first is true and must still appear (case 007).

conformance_note: A, B and C must produce different outputs against one bundle: PASS+finding, PASS+finding, FAIL. An evaluator returning FAIL for B has collapsed `within` into `hold`; one returning no corpus finding for A and B cannot surface the class at all, since neither has a false assertion to catch. That is the point of H1 — the evaluator alone cannot close it, and the static gate and the event-catalogue completeness check are the other two thirds.
